It is built around three of the most consequential data frontiers in environmental science today: Exposing Ocean Pollution at Scale Be part of the conversation around SkyTruth's groundbreaking new report revealing the extent, concentration, & culpability of chronic oil pollution in our oceans - a major advancement for mapping human industrial activity at sea & an essential step towards holding polluters accountable. About the host: SkyTruth (skytruth.org) is a conservation technology nonprofit that leverages satellite imagery & environmental data to create tools & develop insights that drive accountability, accelerate climate action, & support biodiversity protection. gary_2026_09_23_accommodating_growth_in_.summary: Gary's Guide: All guests are welcome to arrive early for a light lunch & networking beginning around noon. Most of the world's urban growth over the next few decades will happen in cities that don't yet exist at scale - concentrated in the Global South, where population growth is fastest & infrastructure is least locked in. Whether that growth compounds sprawl-driven emissions or avoids them depends on choices being made right now about housing & land use policy, as well as transportation infrastructure investments. This panel will draw from the experience of urban planning, land use, & transportation experts actively working on efforts in the global south. gary_2026_09_23_visualizing_climate_worl.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_23_visualizing_climate_worl.summary: Gary's Guide: Thanks to a proliferation of climate data, processed & interpreted with AI tools & new visualization methods, we can recognize new patterns in our relationship with our cities & our planet, predict extreme events or future hazards, & inform the hard work of climate adaptation & mitigation. Visualizing Climate Worlds brings together three projects that turn data into new ways of seeing - & living in - a changing planet. The Better Planet Laboratory at CU Boulder uses satellite data, sensors, & AI to monitor global food & environmental systems, transforming planetary-scale information into early-warning & decision tools for a more resilient, equitable future. MIT's Urban Metabolism Environmental Research & Action Lab (UMERA) applies Material Flow Analysis & machine learning to 11,000+ cities worldwide, surfacing productive & sometimes unexpected climate sister-city networks & modeling how they converge on unique sustainability paths to 2050. And BEAM Studio's TIDELANDS 2100 draws on NOAA flood models & the oral histories of Rhode Island's coastal residents to build immersive VR worlds of adaptation in place. Together they move from planetary monitoring to urban comparison to lived experience, asking: once we can model & see a changing planet, how do we choose to live in it? More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

jc_culture_10004824_2026_09_26_the_socie.title: The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) 91st Annual Members Exhibition 2026
jc_culture_10004824_2026_09_26_the_socie.label: Art / Culture
jc_culture_10004824_2026_09_26_the_socie.place: MANA CONTEMPORARY, 888 NEWARK AVE., JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004824_2026_09_26_the_socie.summary: 91st Annual Members Exhibition The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is excited to announce its upcoming 91st Annual Members Exhibition, to be held at Mana Contemporary in Jersey City from September 11–27, 2026 (Fridays and Saturdays, 3:00–7:00 PM; Sundays, 12:00–3:00 PM). The exhibition will feature 200 hand-pulled prints representing a broad range of printmaking techniques and subjects, created by SAGA artists from across the country. Awards will be juried by Leslie Diuguid, founder of Du-Good Press in Brooklyn. The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is a nonprofit organization established in 1915 whose mission is to promote contemporary printmakers, cultivate printmaking appreciation and education, and provide a collaborative and inclusive platform for artists across the country. https://sagaprints.com/ Hosting this year’s exhibition is Monira Foundation, an independent nonprofit institution that functions as a radical experimental laboratory, working in close collaboration with artists, curators, musicians, dancers, producers, and writers to conceive, realize, and present innovative projects in all media. Monira is located within Mana Contemporary, a 2-million-square-foot art center. The complex occupies a renovated 100-year-old former tobacco warehouse, featuring expansive exhibition spaces, working artist studios, the International Center of Photography archives, and more. A free public reception and awards ceremony with participating artists will be held on Saturday, September 26, from 3:00–5:00 PM. Guests are invited to enjoy light refreshments while celebrating the diversity and innovation of contemporary printmaking. WHEN Exhibition: Fridays–Sundays, September 11–27, 2026 Public Reception & Awards Ceremony: Saturday, September 26, 2026 3:00–5:00 PM WHERE Mana Contemporary 888 Newark Avenue Jersey City, NJ 07306

jc_culture_44040_2026_10_03_free_diapers.summary: Please Take Our Ad: Community Giving Luvs is bringing its Give Back Billboard to Jersey City, turning an advertisement into an opportunity to directly support local families with free diapers. As the packs are removed, the billboard will gradually reveal the message: “Leak protection shouldn’t be a luxury.” For 50 years, Luvs has stood for value, and as families face the rising cost of raising children, the brand is bringing that commitment directly to the community through free diapers, giveaways and more. One free box of diapers per household, while supplies last. Sizes subject to availability. No purchase necessary.
